utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Traldi, we were informed that you had a matter -- a preliminary matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honours. I'll be using one document this morning that wasn't on the list for the witness. I had listed 65 ter 20414, it's an intercept. In checking our records last night, I realised that the transcripts are in evidence as P6904 and Mr. Stojanovic and I have agreed that we'll use the version that's already in evidence rather than duplicating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. That is hereby on the record. Good morning, Mr. Sajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sajic, before we continue I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraph 14 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now Exhibit D836.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- you say: "In April 1992, I became the secretary of the ARK Secretariat for National Defence." You were appointed to that position by the ARK Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: End of April, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you say in paragraph 16 of D836 that part of your job as secretary of the secretariat was to be a link between the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence and the municipal secretariats. I want to ask you just a couple of questions about what that meant. First, being a link meant transmitting communications and orders from the Ministry of Defence to the municipal secretariats; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it meant providing assistance to the municipal secretariats; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a position to provide assistance and that was not a task that was specifically assigned to me. Because at that time I was commander of the Territorial Defence of Banja Luka, and I could not really cover two posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you were serving the function as secretary of the secretariat, was part of your responsibility to assist municipal secretariats of national Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that my obligation was to convey what the ministry wanted. I really didn't have the capacity to provide any particular assistance. I didn't even visit these secretariats. I did not go from one municipality to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we have 65 ter 31670, page 46.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, this will be another part of your Brdjanin testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm looking for the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Beginning at line 17, you're asked: "What were your job responsibilities as -- in this new position that you were appointed to on 27 April 1992?" And before I read your answer, that's the position of secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you answered: "My obligation was to be a link between the Ministry of Defence of the Socialist Republic of B and H, and the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was called," you clarified, "the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was a link between the municipal secretariat and the ministry. It was a link, a bypass, transmitting communications, orders, providing assistance to the municipality secretariats." Do you stand behind this portion of your Brdjanin testimony as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have this in the Serbian version. However, I have understood the interpretation of what you said and it is a fact that that is what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you confirm today that what you stated in the Brdjanin case was truthful, in the portion that I just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean providing assistance, that is relatively part of my statement too; but, all right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the functions of the Secretariat for National Defence also included recruitment for the army; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it is the municipal secretariats that were in charge, not regional.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And did the municipal secretariats also keep records of men who served in the army?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the only records that were kept; that is to say, at the municipal secretariats. That is to say, records of men and of materiel. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn back now to the ARK Crisis Staff. Sir, in paragraph 63 of D836, you say it is "incorrect that an ARK Crisis Staff was covertly formed on the 22nd of January, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In this respect, I'd like to look at 65 ter 20578.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, this is a transcript of an intercepted conversation between Radovan Karadzic and Jovan Cizmovic dated the 22nd of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 6 in the English and 7 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the statement is rather ambiguous in its language. He is saying it is correct, I have no knowledge. I mean, if have you no knowledge then it's very difficult to say that something is incorrect. But that's statement-taking which is confusing rather than enlightening. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And -- not certain we have the right page in the English. And I'd asked for page 6 which may have been my mistake. Can we confirm we've got that one. Seven in the B/C/S and 6 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They are both in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'd had the correct English page a moment ago. So the B/C/S is now correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, not anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the left, we had -- on the left of our screen for the B/C/S we had the right page, and now the right page for the English. This is the right page, Mr. Traldi, in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The B/C/S is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The English is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, looking at -- it's the fifth, I believe, full quote there, Mr. Cizmovic is saying in this intercepted conversation from 22 January: "Tonight we also established the Crisis Staff, which will act when nobody can get together, when they can assemble more quickly." So a Crisis Staff was formed in the ARK on the 22nd of January; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In my view, it wasn't established. This thing that Cizmovic is saying, this, in this conversation, that doesn't have to mean anything. I mean, I haven't any -- seen any document of the 22nd and I cannot accept this. I can only accept that I don't know, but ... I've never heard of this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 20578.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I take it that Madam Registrar is waiting for the audio CD. Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 20578 receives number P6971, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in paragraph 36, sir, you say you attended some meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff. When you didn't attend, would someone attend in your place?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have that in B/C/S? All of this is in English. And they keep showing it in English to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, to the extent there's B/C/S, it will be shown to you. To the extent there's no B/C/S, it will be translated for you. So if you wait and not get upset about it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you attended some meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you didn't attend, one of your subordinates in the TO would attend in your place; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Maybe, but I'm not sure. That's not the way it was in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you remember Mr. Topic replacing you at such meetings several times?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the municipal or the Crisis Staff of the AR Krajina? There were two.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's take them one by one. Did Mr. Topic ever replace you at municipal Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Topic was the number two man in the Territorial Defence; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did he ever replace you at ARK Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to make a correction here. Kesic was number two, not Topic, but never mind. I don't know whether he stood in for me at the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. Did Kesic ever stand in for you at the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, when one of your subordinates attended a Crisis Staff meeting for you, do you remember if they'd tell you what happened at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not really attach particular importance to the AR Krajina Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for this obligation, it wasn't really a major obligation that we had towards the AR Krajina Crisis Staff. Actually, we didn't have one at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was not whether you found it important. The question was not whether it was an obligation. The question is whether if one of your immediate subordinates had been present, whether they told you what happened during such meetings. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the answer to the question, that they did report that to you. Mr. Traldi, could you look at page 8, line 7 and seek whether you can -- Before you, in your previous answer, said that you did not really attach particular importance, part of what you said was missing. Do you remember what you said before you said that it was not particularly important for you; and, if so, would you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What you said before you answered that the Crisis Staff meetings were -- that you did not really attach particular importance to that. The interpreters told us that they missed a line which you said before saying this. If you don't remember, we'll proceed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Like your subordinates would sometimes attend in your place, when General Talic couldn't attend ARK Crisis Staff meetings, the assistant commander of the 1st Krajina Corps for civilian affairs, Colonel Vujinovic, would attend the meetings; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Colonel Vujinovic at meetings, Talic only once. Colonel Vujinovic was not a member of the Crisis Staff. He was more of an observer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've answered several questions but not the one that I asked. When General Talic couldn't attend, that's when Colonel Vujinovic would attend on behalf of the corps; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On behalf of the corps, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And like your subordinates would be responsible to tell you what had happened at the meeting, Colonel Vujinovic would be responsible to inform General Talic about what happened when he attended a Crisis Staff meeting and General Talic could not; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now while the ARK Crisis Staff was meet, the ARK Assembly wasn't meeting; right

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the assembly sat during those months. Maybe, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let me ask it this way: It was the ARK Crisis Staff that was issuing decisions in the Bosnian Krajina in May and June of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some decisions that were made by the Crisis Staff and some conclusions were reached, but since the Crisis Staff of the AR Krajina was not accepted as some kind of organ, then --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the end of the sentence again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please come a bit closer to the microphone and repeat the last part of your answer. You said that: "Since the Crisis Staff of the ARK was not accepted as some kind of an organ, then ..." And could you tell us what you then said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then they couldn't pass decisions on behalf of the -- of the Assembly of the AR Krajina. There was the Executive Council, and these decisions that were made were not accepted by all municipalities. And decisions were being reached, so the answer would be, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all microphones please be switched off when the witness is speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let have first 65 ter 31672, page 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be another part of your Brdjanin testimony. And again, the transcript will be in English and I'll read it out to you. Beginning at line 6 you're asked -- let's begin at line 7: "Just one more question. I don't have the exact page reference but you'll agree with me that during the time the ARK Crisis Staff met, the ARK Assembly was not meeting; correct? If you need to, we can dig it out of your transcript." You responded: "I don't think so. I don't think it was correct." And you were asked: "... so it was the ARK Crisis Staff that was issuing decisions in the Krajina in June of 1992; correct?" And you answered: "Yes." Do you confirm today that it was the ARK Crisis Staff that was issuing the decisions on its own authority in the Krajina in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Decisions, yes. Now, whether they could do that on the basis of the law, no. Made decisions, yes. And the decisions were being published too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you said in an answer a moment ago - and you say in your statement - that some municipalities did not accept the ARK Crisis Staff's decisions. I'll look at a few examples later this morning. But before we do that, in fact, you can only speak about Banja Luka and you don't know the extent to which other municipalities in the ARK implemented ARK Crisis Staff conclusions; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to ask you now about some of the statements made by Mr. Brdjanin, the president of the Crisis Staff. In paragraph 42, you say that you don't know whether and why Brdjanin said in the media that only a thousand Muslims would be allowed to stay in Banja Luka to clean the streets, but you'd heard from others that he did say this. I have several questions in this respect. First, you heard this from Serbs in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard that, this sentence of 1.000 Muslims. And this is something that my brain will never accept. But that I heard all sorts of things being said, that's true, but this thing, 1.000 Muslims, no. I mean, if I'm forced to say yes, then --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not understand the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, you're not forced to say anything. You only have an obligation to tell us the truth. The question was not whether you could possibly think it to be true, but since in your statement we read that you heard others saying that this is what Mr. Brdjanin had said, the question was whether you heard this from Serbs in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I talked about this to the investigator too and for a long time at that. Brdjanin was saying all sorts of things. That's true. But I did not hear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness -- stop. I stop you there. In your statement, you said that you heard from others that Brdjanin had said this. Now, whether these others were telling the truth or not is a different matter. But the question is: Who were those that had told you that Brdjanin had said this? Were they Serbs from Banja Luka? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But in your statement recently you said that you heard this from others but you have no idea who told you this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31671, page 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this will be another part of your Brdjanin testimony. Now, beginning on line 19 at the bottom of the page, you're asked: "I want to ask you a little bit about some of the things Mr. Brdjanin said when he was president of the ARK Crisis Staff, and perhaps just before he became president as well. One of the things you were asked about in this interview that you remembered was hearing from other Serbs that Mr. Brdjanin had said in the media - doesn't say whether it's TV or radio - that only a thousand Muslims will be allowed to stay in Banja Luka and that those thousand Muslims will be comprised of elderly people who will put to cleaning the streets." And you were asked: "Now, do you remember hearing about that from Serbs in Banja Luka, that they had heard Mr. Brdjanin say that in the media, as you state in the interview?" And you responded: "Yes." Does this portion of your sworn Brdjanin testimony refresh your recollection as to whether Serbs in Banja Luka had told you that they heard Mr. Brdjanin say this in the media?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember who told me. I communicated with -- with Croats and Muslims. It's possible that it was also Serbs. I'm not denying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Next, you say in your statement that Muslims and Croats in Banja Luka were "certainly disturbed by such statements." What you mean specifically is that they were made to be afraid; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a part of that, but they were disturbed because of more serious things, but one of the reasons was also this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this statement, that only a small number of elderly Muslims could stay in Banja Luka to sweep the streets, this is a derogatory statement about Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while you didn't -- while your evidence is that you didn't hear Mr. Brdjanin say this specifically, you can confirm that Mr. Brdjanin made these types of derogatory speeches in the media; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 03277.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 41 of D836 you say you don't believe that Mr. Brdjanin personally called for the dismissal of Muslims and Croats from work in Banja Luka. Now, this is a decision by the ARK Crisis Staff dated the 26th of May, 1992. Directing your attention to point 3, we read: "Leading posts in social and public organisations may be occupied only by the most professional persons who are absolutely devoted to the Serbian people in the Serbian Republic Bosnia and Herzegovina." And that meant Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same thing today. The party that wins will appoint its own cadre. There were also loyal Muslims and Croats, loyal to Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'll get to that in a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But before I do, I tender 65 ter 03277.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 3277 receives number P6972, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P6948.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a decision by the ARK Crisis Staff dated the 22nd of June, 1992, and it's signed by Mr. Brdjanin. And directing your attention to the first point, we read: "Only personnel of Serbian ethnicity may hold executive post, posts where the information flow is possible, and posts involving the protection of socially owned property ..." And then at the end of that first point, we read: "Likewise, these posts may not be held by those employees of Serbian ethnicity who have not confirmed it in the plebiscite or have not yet accepted that the only representative of the Serbian people is the Serbian Democratic Party." So here Mr. Brdjanin is quite explicitly signing a document that calls for Muslims and Croats to be dismissed from their positions; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Democratic Party had complete power which it won in the elections, and it appointed its own cadres. The same principle applies today, that the requirement that the cadres even have to be members of the SDS. So automatically if somebody was a Muslim and a director, they could not be a director any longer. They could be something else but not a director. This is just one example.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I appreciate that additional detail, sir. But directly relevant to your statement, this document shows that through his position as president of the ARK Crisis Staff, Mr. Brdjanin, in fact, did personally call for the dismissal of Muslims and Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that he said dismiss them, but he just said that they could not occupy executive posts. But I don't see it written anywhere that they ought to be dismissed. The decision on appointment of cadres was made by the Executive Board. They would sign the decision, unless there was some kind of abuse of power. But a director, if he's no longer a director, could do something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To implement this decision, that only personnel of Serbian ethnicity may hold executive posts, it is would be necessary for Muslims and Croats who held executive posts and these other types of posts described in point I to stop holding those posts; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who were in leadership positions or places where information was coming in or being disseminated and were not Serbs were to be replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you also saw this document in your Karadzic testimony, and I'd like to look at that for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we 65 ter 31673, page 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were asked similarly: "Okay. Well, at paragraph 41," same statement, "you said you did not believe that Brdjanin personally called for the dismissal of Muslims and Croats, but this document shows that through his position as ARK Crisis Staff president he did exactly that, called for the dismissal of Muslims and Croats; right?" And you answered: "From the documents it appears so." First, do you stand by that portion of your sworn Karadzic testimony as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we could change the play of words here. Replacement and dismissal is not the same thing. Even when we were talking a little bit earlier, I would say, yes, they were being relieved from their posts but it's not dismissal. And it doesn't say dismissal. I don't know if anybody dismissed anybody, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you -- if you replace one person by another, then that one person does not hold that post any further. To that extent, he's out. Let me just use ordinary language. Do you know what happened with those who were out for these reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Many stayed in the same company doing different work, in a different job. Your Honours, many stayed at work. Many did leave. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "many stayed." Could you give us the function and the names of some persons in executive positions who stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was in the Meridijan. I cannot remember his name. His name was Hilmija and he was in the Meridijan company. He was replaced but he remained employed. He still worked in that company and he worked there for a long time until he left. But in 1992 he was working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What was his new position? What was his new position in that firm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember. It was a less important job. They would get less important positions, less important ones. Perhaps they were an advisor or some kind of assistant or a clerk. Something that was less important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And he was of what ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A Bosniak, Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you have any other names, please write them down during the break - that is, company and the name of that executive -- that person in an executive position - so that we can consider facts in this respect. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before we leave this topic, sir, in paragraph 41 of D836, you say in pertinent part: "I can agree, however, that in 1992 Muslims and Croats were dismissed from work." Do you stand behind that portion of your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we get paragraph 41 of D836 on the screen, please. We have the right part of the English, yes. And in the B/C/S, I think it will be the top of the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you say, in pertinent part: "I can agree, however, that in 1992 Muslims and Croats were dismissed from work." This is in your witness statement which you swore was truthful and accurate in this case which you also swore was truthful and accurate in the Karadzic case. Do you stand behind this portion of your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but I think that it would be good to read the entire sentence to the witness and not just a part of it and that way just take it out of the -- out of context. Perhaps then the witness can respond to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you're doing what has been done so many times, that is to, more or less, give signals to the witness, which you should not do. If there's any matter, if you say, I would appreciate if Mr. Traldi would give context or more context, that message is clear enough for Mr. Traldi. And if he doesn't understand it or if he considers it better not to do that at that moment, you have a possibility in re-examination to deal with the matter. Mr. Traldi, I don't know whether you find it a good suggestion or not, but we leave it to that at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm happy to read the whole sentence. But I will be asking the witness specifically again whether he confirms the portion I read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the full sentence is: "I can agree, however, that in 1992 Muslims and Croats were dismissed from work, but I do not agree that the Crisis Staff was fully responsible for that because Serbs were also dismissed." Now, do you confirm what you say in this sentence that in 1992 Muslims and Croats were dismissed from work?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you permit me, I read the entire sentence, and it has a completely different meaning than the question that was put to me. Completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness -- Witness. Mr. Stojanovic, you see now what is the result of how you operate. I don't need any further -- I've just established this. Witness, the question simply was whether you still confirm that in 1992 Muslims and Croats were dismissed from work.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi. Mr. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless you have any objection against one of the questions or if you have any legitimate reason to interfere, you may do so, but not to further comment on what I just said. That's what you're not allowed to do. If there's anything else, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with all due respect, I just wanted to say for the transcript that I did not have the intention as was placed here. I -- in the transcript, I just put that for purposes of context and I wish to say that for the transcript. I did not have any erroneous goals or objectives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could have done so at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or malicious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said that you're supposed to not to further comment on what I said. And the only thing I said is not that you intentionally did it. I said this the result of what you did. I didn't even discuss the intentions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Serbs you say in that sentence were also dismissed were those not loyal to the SDS as reflected in your comments earlier this morning and Mr. Brdjanin's decision that we just looked at; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Relatedly, you say in paragraph 43 of D836 that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you go to paragraph 43, I just have a question. You're saying that the Crisis Staff was not fully responsible for the dismissal. Who was -- who had dismissed these Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The companies. The leadership of the company. And the companies either accepted or did not accept the decisions of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The decision of the Crisis Staff as contained in Mr. Brdjanin's decision that was referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have one additional question. You say the Crisis Staff was not fully responsible. But that decision should be implemented. And if you would not implement it, you'd be fired yourself, isn't it? That's what the decision says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would need to read the decision again, but I wouldn't have -- I wasn't dismissed and I didn't fulfil the -- implement the decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Whether that was given effect, yes or no, is a different matter. But let's have a look at the decision again so that you can read it. And it was -- Could you please assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: P6948, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm drawing your attention to point III. And in relation to that, also point II, the deadline for the fulfilment of the tasks given was 26th of June. That's four days after the decision was issued. And then III reads: "Failure to comply with the above mentioned decision shall automatically result in the dismissal of the responsible persons." Now, Mr. Sajic, if you say that there is no full responsibility for the Crisis Staff, would you agree with me that if there's such a clear threat, that if you don't do what is ordered, that this gives at least great part, if not all, of the responsibility to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it's a question of replacing people, not dismissing them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not a question of dismissal. That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you agree with me that not doing what is order tells you is heavily sanctioned and that that -- but please tell us whether you agree or not. And that makes the Crisis Staff very responsible for any result of what they decided.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Crisis Staff didn't have the instruments to apply any sanctions. None. Other than the fact that Brdjanin signed a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So -- so you say so this is distributed but everyone just thinks, Well, why would we care, because it's just the Crisis Staff. We don't do it. Is that your position in interpreting this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not interpreting it like that, Your Honour. This is how I interpret it, if you permit me to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Briefly, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Crisis Staff made a decision and disseminated it to all publicly-owned enterprises, so the usual thing would be that these replacements would be carried out. But if they were not, they were perhaps not expecting -- they were not complying with the decision of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last two sentences of what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last two sentences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The decision that publicly-owned and other companies and institutions received was implemented to a significant degree but not everyone complied with the decision. They did not dismiss the people in question but they would assign them to other jobs. Some of them. And so the Crisis Staff could not apply any punitive measures or any punishment because of this action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you say you -- you earlier said you didn't implement these -- this decision or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who was it that you kept in an executive position and who was of Croat or Muslim ethnicity which you did not replace in your organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my organisation at the TO Staff, I did not replace anyone. Zoran Kolak was my security chief for security of buildings. I didn't replace him. He was a Croat. Zdenko Mesud; the first one was a Croat, the second one was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And they stayed until when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They stayed as long as I did. Afterwards, they moved into brigades. I stopped on the 15th of June, de facto and de jure, whatever you wish, and they went to the units of the Serb republic, the light brigades. And they went there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you said you did not implement this decision because they stayed, and you said that they stayed until the 15th of June. That's what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's how long I was their commander. Later on, they stayed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the decision was of the 22nd of June. So if you were not in your position anymore, then it was -- there was no question about implementing or not. Because what happened until the 15th of June could not be covered by a decision of the 22nd of June, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. They continued in the light brigades after the 15th of June. That's an extension of the Territorial Defence. That's what I meant when I said that. They continued along this path. In the brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you said is: I wasn't dismissed, and I didn't implement the decisions. We [sic] are talking about what happened 15th of June; whereas, we are talking about a decision issued on the 22nd of June. Leave it to that. If there's any follow-up questions, Mr. Traldi, I leave it to you. We'll first take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to be brought in, Mr. Stojanovic, have you checked the adjudicated facts as we advised you to do yesterday, whether they are, indeed, for the full 100 percent the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We tried, Your Honour, and I think that we can inform you about the checks that we carried out. To the best of our understanding, I will tell you in the briefest possible terms. Adjudicated facts as marked 416, 427, 430, 431, 433, and 456 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it seems that they are absolutely identical. Adjudicated fact 447 in the Karadzic case, though, has a phrase in its first sentence and that goes beyond what is contained in the Mladic adjudicated facts. The words are as follows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, of course, we identified that already quite a while ago. What we want you to be aware of that there are differences and that you didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- verify that exactly at the beginning and the same is true for 421, that was overturned by the Appeals Chamber. 447 was rephrased. And we expect you to take adequate action on those differences. But are there any others apart from 421 and 447 which you identified as being different?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then take adequate action for that because the witness, of course, commented on the adjudicated facts as phrased in his statement rather than as the adjudicated facts as phrased in this case. Mr. Traldi, if you're ready, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, returning to the topic of dismissals, you say in paragraph 43 of your statement that you: "... do not deny that Croatian and Muslim officers were dismissed from the 1st Krajina Corps." In fact, you can confirm that Croatian and Muslim officers were purged from the 1st Krajina Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Purged?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "Purged" is the word I used, yes.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31672, page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up this will be another portion of your Brdjanin testimony. Again it will appear in English and I'll read it out to you. Now, the question here -- you're referred to a document, and the question I'm interested begins on line 23. You were asked: "Now you know, don't you, that in fact ultimately not right on this day, but soon thereafter officers of Muslim and Croat [sic] nationality were purged from the 1st Krajina Corps correct?"

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say: "I'm not trying to deny that but I do not know the exact date when these officers were purged or who exactly was purged. I don't know the date, whether it was on the same day or not. I can see this order by Mladic, and it looks quite clear to me." And you were asked: "I'm not asking you for the day; I just wanted your confirmation that it in fact occurred, that these men of Muslim and Croat nationality were, in fact, purged from the 1st Krajina Corps ranks. Correct? Don't worry about the exact day." And you answered: "Yes." Do you stand behind this portion of your testimony in the Brdjanin case as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This notion of purging is something I find unclear. Dismissal and reassignment is something different. That's why I react and said no. As for this interpretation of yours, I'm not sure whether it is dismissal or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the essence is whether officers of Muslim and Croat nationality were dismissed from their jobs in the 1st Krajina Corps. Were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Active-duty officers, yes. On orders they were transferred. Up until the end of the war. They were on leave and then they were reassigned. And reserve officers stayed. Reserve officers. All of them are officers, reserve officers, active-duty officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well that officers of Muslim and Croat nationality who were put on leave, that they returned after the war? Is that -- in their old positions? Is that what you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I'm telling you that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to communications. Sir, you discuss communications between the ARK and Pale in your statement and you mention the regional communication centre in Banja Luka. The regional centre in Banja Luka was already connected with the republican centre by the 23rd of March, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it should have been, but then I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P4088.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a document coming from the SDS dated the 23rd of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you assist us in finding the right paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The third paragraph in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I mean paragraph in the statement because -- unless you are not referring to any paragraph in the statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He discusses communications at some length. The regional communications centre, I'm afraid I don't have the paragraph in front of me. It's a brief reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll try to find it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The third paragraph here reads: "Regional centres in Banja Luka, Trebinje, Sokolac, and Bijeljina are already connected with the republican centre of TT and radio communications ..." So it's correct, isn't it, that by the 23rd of March, 1992 the regional communications centre in Banja Luka was connected with the republican communications centre?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 10743.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an article in Glas dated the 9th of May, 1992, entitled: "Information Blockade Lifted." It includes a number of quotes from Zeljko Katic, and he was the head of the regional information centre; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Zeljko Katic was in that centre. I know him but I'm not sure whether he actually headed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Looking at the second paragraph in the article we read that as of 9th of May: "The regional information centre is operating 24 hours a day non-stop."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And turning to page 2 in the English near the top and the second column in the B/C/S of the same article.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read that among its other responsibilities, the regional communications centre was: "... directly connecting the leadership of the municipality with the Autonomous Region of Krajina." That was one of the regional information centre's functions; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its function was always communication between Sarajevo and Banja Luka, and that's the way it remained. It was not communication between municipalities. Secretariats, yes. Somebody from the AR Krajina probably used this, either the Executive Council or the Crisis Staff. So if you have a centre through which you can send a dispatch, then people do use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 10743.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10743 receives number P6973, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P3027. And I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an order Minister of Defence Subotic issued on the 16th of April, 1992. Among other things, under "decision," it calls for: "A general, public mobilisation ... on the entire territory." Now, you implemented this order; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you answer the question, whether you implemented this order, especially on the part Mr. Traldi read to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph number 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The part I read to you was: "A general, public mobilisation has been ordered on the entire territory of SBH." You implemented this order and specifically that point in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps for the witness to be able to read it, it's at the bottom of the page under number 2, so the second "odluku" but then under 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How about going to the end? I didn't even see this. I looked at the first one, not the second one. The decision, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason why I invited you to read the latter part. Start reading at 2 at the bottom of the page. And then the question is whether you implemented this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you had to have communications with Pale to receive this order; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: How could you have received this order if you couldn't receive communications from Pale?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was probably provided to me by someone as a dispatch from that centre. I never entered the centre during the war. I never said dispatches to Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me rephrase my question. For you to implement this order, it was necessary for the Autonomous Region of Krajina to have communications with Pale where the order was issued; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision was not published anywhere. It was submitted to me through --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let's keep matters simple. In order to implement it, you must have received it. In order to receive it, there must be a way of communication between Pale and you. That's the question, whether you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in fact there was an operating teleprinter connection between Pale and Banja Luka at this point, the 16th of April, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness. Could all unnecessary microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you repeat your answer, please, Witness, speaking into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31682.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a decision from the ARK Crisis Staff dated THE 15th of May, 1992, signed by Mr. Brdjanin and type-signed by you. Turning to page 2 in the B/C/S and still on 1 -- or beginning on 1 in the English, we see a list of issues on which reports should be submitted as specified at the top of the text to the ARK Crisis Staff via the district reporting centre. So as of 15 May 1992 via the district reporting centre, the Crisis Staff in the ARK had communications with municipal organs; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see who it was sent to. I just see this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here in the first point, we read: "In order to ensure continual insight into the situation on the territory of the AR Krajina and a framework for adopting decisions by the Crisis Staff, the municipal organs are required to report to the district organs, and they should report to the AR Krajina Crisis Staff operative on duty, via the district reporting centre ..." This is a decision issued on the 15th of May. What I'm putting to you is: At that point, the district reporting centre was functioning and the municipal organs were capable of issuing reports in the way that you and Mr. Brdjanin are deciding they should do here; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some had the ability, others did not. Some municipalities that did not have printers could not file reports. But generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I tender 65 ter 31682.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31682 receives number P6974, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P6904.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: While this comes up, sir, you claim that the ARK and the central republican authorities had substantial differences and that the ARK Crisis Staff was not the highest organ of authority in the ARK because of its differences with the leadership in Pale. Now, this is a transcript of an intercepted phone conversation between President Karadzic and Mr. Brdjanin on the 1st of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 4 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: President Karadzic tells Brdjanin, in pertinent part: "Call me about something that you cannot resolve. You have all the power in Krajina. Why don't you exercise this power?" Now, President Karadzic is recognizing Mr. Brdjanin's authority in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the line? I cannot see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you see where about six lines from the bottom, President Karadzic is -- asks: Can you solve a single problem without Karadzic. It's two of President Karadzic's statements below that, so the second line from the bottom. The second quote from the bottom, starts: "But no, no, it is not that I can't." And there's a -- there's a cursor next to it on the screen at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's -- it's next to what looks like a little magnifying-glass on the screen, sir. So my question for you about this line is simple: When President Karadzic says to Mr. Brdjanin, "You have all the power in Krajina. Why don't you exercise this power?" he is recognizing that Mr. Brdjanin has substantial power in the Autonomous Region of Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Significant," "substantial," and "all" is not the same thing. The authority was in the Executive Council. They are accusing each other, the Crisis Staff, the Executive Council. This happened once some went to complain to Karadzic. They actually gossiped about each other. And when he said, "You have all the power," he didn't mean just Brdjanin having all the power. This is at least what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, turning to page 5 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S, and it's seventh or eighth line down right below Mr. Brdjanin utters the single word "Kupresanin."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: President Karadzic is speaking very directly to Mr. Brdjanin and he says: "Come on, man, do your job. Don't call me about every minor problem. I'm not your nanny. You have power in your hands, and you have presidents of municipalities through whom you can exercise this power ..." He's speaking directly to Mr. Brdjanin there; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand this as a conversation between Radoslav Brdjanin and Radovan Karadzic in which they refer to Mr. Kupresanin, and in this case he's using the president of the region, Kupresanin, as a personality, as a function, and where Karadzic says that they should call the president of the municipalities, he meant that the region should do that. Kupresanin or somebody else. I don't see that Brdjo could do that. And if he did do that, I don't see that all of that was done the way it was supposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your interpretation is based solely on having read the text of this paragraph just now because you were not privy to any conversations between President Karadzic and Mr. Brdjanin yourself; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, of course, you're asking questions to the witness in a similar vein by saying do you confirm that he is recognizing that Mr. Brdjanin has substantial power. You're inviting the witness to interpret it. So then, don't be surprised if he comes with an interpretation and then you put to him you have no knowledge about it. That's a bit odd in my view. Let's -- I have one other question. Is there any reason why you say the date is the 1st of November, whereas the document says it's the 31st of October?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My notes may be in error, Mr. President, and I'll check and respond at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Related to exercising power through the presidents of the municipalities, in paragraph 50, you mention that you had the impression --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Paragraph 50 of D836.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- that meetings of presidents of municipalities would be held on Mondays. These were meetings between the presidents of municipalities in the ARK and the ARK Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: These Monday meetings were held regularly; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't attend every meeting. They were quite frequent. But I don't know about regular.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, just for clarity, let's have 65 ter 31672, page 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Another portion of your Brdjanin testimony. Sorry, I've called up the wrong portion of your Brdjanin testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's been uploaded under three numbers. If I could have just one second, Your Honour. If we have 31671, page 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were asked about the Monday morning meetings with the presidents of the various municipalities. And then, beginning at line 11, you say -- you're asked, rather: "And you stated later on, it's not particularly important, that you remembered that these Monday meetings were regular. Right? On page 72 of the English." And you responded: "Yes." So it's correct, as you testified in the Brdjanin case, that these Monday morning meetings were regular; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a translation but if that's what I said, that's what I thought at the time. I wasn't at all the meetings, but it's possible that they were. I mean, perhaps they were held every Monday. Saints' Days were occurring as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One of the purposes of the meetings was that so presidents of municipalities could go back to their municipalities and brief those municipalities on what was concluded or discussed at the ARK Crisis Staff meetings; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the reason was. I really cannot say. Who would he inform about the presidents?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I was putting to you was that the presidents of these municipalities would inform their municipal Crisis Staffs or their Municipal Executive Boards about what was being decided and discussed at the ARK Crisis Staff meetings. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, the people who were supposed to be there were the presidents of the Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the question then was whether they were invited to pass on to the local Crisis Staffs or their Municipal Executive Boards what had been decided in the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know how they were summoned, what was the way that they were summoned. I know that it would -- was a meeting without any agenda and they, as presidents of municipalities, and at the same time the presidents of their Crisis Staffs, probably once they returned to their municipality, I assume, I'm not sure, I don't know, I cannot assert this 100 per cent, they would call the president of the Crisis Staff, the members of the inner circle, and then they would say, Well, that was what was discussed. That would be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, in paragraphs 55 through 58 of D836, you discuss a meeting of the ARK Crisis Staff where the Prijedor representatives discussed facilities that you referred to as collection centres and investigation centres. Was this one of the Monday meetings where representatives from different municipalities were present?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was 20 years ago. But, probably, yes, it -- if it was. I mean, if it means anything to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin chaired this meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Prijedor representatives were Milomir Stakic, Simo Drljaca, and Slobodan Kuruzovic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you testified earlier that if General Talic was not present at a Crisis Staff meet, Colonel Vujinovic would attend instead. Do you recall who attended this session on behalf of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Vujinovic attended usually, but I don't know about that particular case, whether he was there or not. I don't know what I said. I don't know if he was there on that occasion or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, at this meeting it was clear to you and the other people there that there were large numbers of people being held in what you called collection centres in the ARK at that time; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was known that there was a number of people in the collection centre. I don't know exactly how many. I knew that something was happening in the area of Prijedor and that there was a collection centre. I didn't know what the number of people was. And I think that nobody at the meeting ever specifically said that there was such and such a number of people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was clear that the people being held in those centres were non-Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You mention in your statement that Predrag Radic later went to Omarska and that he told you he was upset by what he saw there. I have a few questions specifically about what he told you. First, Mr. Radic told you about his visit about a day after he'd been to the camp; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps that afternoon. Perhaps in the afternoon on that day or the next day. But in any case, it was quite soon after.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're aware that Radoslav Brdjanin and Mr. Vukic were also part of the delegation; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think that that was the delegation. I don't know if anybody else was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall if anyone else was present when you had this conversation with Mr. Radic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I know Radic went and Vukic. I don't know about anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And setting aside the details of the conversation you had in Radic -- you had with Radic, you know as you sit there today that Omarska in 1992 was a terrible place for the prisoners held there and that crimes were committed against the people who were held there; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I found out later, about crimes being committed, yes, I did know that crimes were committed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the end of your statement, you challenge a number of adjudicated facts, and I'm going to address a couple of those now. First, in paragraph 68 of your statement, D836, you state that: "Restrictions on free movement were aimed at all citizens regardless of their nationality." Now, in fact, with the possible exception of Banja Luka, you don't really know about the restrictions that were placed on the movement of non-Serbs in ARK municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what I wrote in the mobilisation order and the order implementing the curfew. And this was applied in Banja Luka to a substantial degree. I emphasise "to a substantial degree." But I don't know how that was implemented in other municipalities. Probably it should have been in the same way as it was implemented in Banja Luka, but I cannot say that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say, sir, that, again with the possible exception of Banja Luka, you don't really know in any detail what kinds of restrictions were placed on the movement of non-Serbs in ARK municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I heard the witness saying yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also heard a "da." You confirmed, Witness, that you don't really know in any detail, apart from Banja Luka, what kinds of restrictions were placed on the movement of non-Serbs in the ARK municipalities. You confirmed that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Next in paragraph 67 of your statement, you state that it is incorrect that the resettlement policy within the Bosnian Krajina was co-ordinated at the regional level by the ARK Crisis Staff. I have a number of questions about this. First, it's true that the ARK Crisis Staff issued decisions on the rules governing people's departures from the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a question. You're asserting that that is so. But it's not a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm asking you if it's true. Can you confirm that the ARK Crisis Staff issued such decisions.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know all the decisions that were made and that were signed. I don't know who made the decisions, who signed them. Perhaps somebody else signed them. As for moving the population out, until the corridor was opened there was no mass transfer of the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question. The question was whether the ARK Crisis Staff issued decisions on the rules governing people's departures from the ARK. That was the question, not whether there were many, or little, or whether it was -- they were implemented, but just decisions being taken by the ARK Crisis Staff on this subject.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It did make some decisions, but I don't know which ones. On that topic, yes, it did make some decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's have P3868. This will be a decision by the ARK Crisis Staff dated the 28th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry. It's a list of conclusions by the ARK Crisis Staff dated the 28th of May, 1992. If we could have point 7 on page 2 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read here: "If Muslims and Croats or members of the SDA or HDZ wish to leave or move out of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, they must enable the endangered Serbian people, against whom unprecedented genocide is being conducted, to move collectively into their places, i.e., they must facilitate an exchange based on reciprocity." So here, the ARK Crisis Staff is setting out rules governing people's departures from the ARK; right.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. This is some story that the SDA and the HDZ as parties allow some of the population to pass through Konjic and the others to come the other way. I mean, this was during the blockade. This is somebody telling a story. It's -- I cannot say what happened. This is a decision relating to prohibition on exchange of foreign currency, so it's -- has to do with giving a permission for people to leave and then not allowing them to go back.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, could you speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This item 7 is part of a - what is it? - a conclusion, something like that. I don't see what the document says, if it's a decision or a conclusion. This point 7 talks about if they want to leave, then the SDA and the HDZ should ensure or make it possible. But these are political parties. They cannot do that. They cannot allow anybody to go or return. All sorts of things were written in these decisions, so somebody put this in a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have D423, page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document again coming from the ARK Crisis Staff and it's reporting that at a meeting of the ARK Crisis Staff on the 29th of May, 1992, the following conclusions were reached. And at point 1, it says: "It has been decided that all Muslims and Croats, who so wish, should be able to move out of the area of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, but on condition that also those Serbs who live outside the Serbian Autonomous Districts and regions are allowed to move into the territories of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Autonomous Region of Krajina. In this manner, an exchange of population, or, more precisely, a resettlement of people from one part of the former SR BH to another would be carried out in an organised manner." We see essentially the same conclusion here as we did in the last document; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read it. Can we go back a little bit, please. No, I didn't receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just an intervention. We have been told that the part that has been put to the witness actually is on the previous page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's have a look at the previous page. In the B/C/S. So ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it now. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So we see here essentially the same conclusion as in the last document; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the relationship is the same: You can leave if our people are allowed to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To come. To move into the places that previously had been inhabited by Muslims and Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone. We cannot hear him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This only refers to this possibility, if across the separation line, across the front line, the combat line, whatever, if it is ensured that ethnic Serbs can arrive who want to leave that territory, and they want that, they say that through the media and whatever, and they're asking someone to help them leave Konjic, Travnik, Sarajevo, wherever, and to leave that territory. Just like Muslims and Croats cannot leave the territory of the AR Krajina because it's blocked. Even if somebody said, You're supposed to leave, how could they leave? It was simply impossible to do that at the time. It was only later in the summer that these organised exchanges started. At this moment, no. So these decisions that were made do not really have any effect -- or these conclusions or...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 08264.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: These are the minutes of the 24th Session of the Petrovac Municipality Crisis Staff dated the 3rd of June, 1992. Petrovac was one of the municipalities in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see here at point 1 a discussion of the conclusions of the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff in Banja Luka. We see at item 1 below that that a man named Bogdan Latinovic read the conclusions of the AR Krajina Crisis Staff in Banja Luka, reached at the session held on 29.05.1992, and then the Crisis Staff of Petrovac municipality gave a proposition for the ARK Crisis Staff's conclusions to be adopted in full as follows. At subpoint 1, we read: "It has been decided that all Muslims and Croats, who so wish be enabled to evacuate from the territory of Autonomous Region of Krajina but only under the condition that the Serbs outside the Serbian Autonomous Regions also be allowed to evacuate to the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is, the Autonomous Region of Krajina. In this way, the organised exchange of population would be carried out, that is its evacuation from one part of the former Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the other."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2, in the B/C/S as well now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read at the bottom of the page in the English and the middle of the page in the B/C/S: "The Crisis Staff has decided to form a board for the implementation of these conclusions, that is on the evacuation of Muslims from the territory of Petrovac municipality." So the Petrovac Crisis Staff thought that these conclusions, in fact, had effect and that they were supposed to begin implementing them, and that's what they did; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's it. That is what was invoked, that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document as the next public Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 8264 receives number P6975, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I see it's time for the break, Mr. President. I am running a little bit behind schedule but I anticipate being done early in the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Early is a rather vague concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's been a little bit difficult to predict the duration. I'd say certainly in the first half of the session and probably in the first quarter, but it depends to some extent on how the examination develops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you give us an indication as to how much time you would need as matters stand now?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this moment, Your Honour, I believe it would be up to 10 minutes.
